summary: 承文帝宽政，平七国之乱，削藩固本；然诛晁错、杀周亚夫，史讥刻薄寡恩。
summary_en: Continuing Wen's lenient course, he put down the Revolt of the Seven States and trimmed the feudatories to steady the throne; yet the deaths of Chao Cuo and Zhou Yafu drew the censure of cold ingratitude.

portrait.appearance_basis: 《汉书》未系统描写景帝形貌。画像宜表现中年君主之态，衣冠从汉初制度，气质沉毅而近于严刻。属艺术想象。

timeline.title: 即位
timeline.summary: 文帝崩，太子启即皇帝位，尊薄太后、窦皇后。
timeline.summary_en: Emperor Wen died; Crown Prince Qi succeeded, honoring Empress Dowager Bo and Empress Dou.

timeline.title: 减笞法
timeline.summary: 定笞刑限度，减轻酷刑，承文帝宽政。
timeline.summary_en: Limits were set on the flogging penalty, easing harsh punishments in the spirit of Emperor Wen.

timeline.title: 晁错议削藩
timeline.summary: 御史大夫晁错建言削吴楚等支郡以尊京师，景帝用其策。
timeline.summary_en: Censor-in-Chief Chao Cuo urged trimming the commanderies of Wu and Chu to exalt the capital; the emperor adopted the plan.

timeline.title: 七国之乱起
timeline.summary: 吴王濞、楚王戊等七国以诛晁错为名举兵西向。
timeline.summary_en: Wu's king Bi, Chu's king Wu, and five others rose and marched west under the pretext of executing Chao Cuo.

timeline.title: 斩晁错于东市
timeline.title_en: Chao Cuo Beheaded at the East Market
timeline.summary: 袁盎说上，斩错以谢吴楚；错死而吴楚兵不止。
timeline.summary_en: At Yuan Ang's persuasion the emperor executed Chao Cuo to appease Wu and Chu; the armies pressed on regardless.

timeline.title: 梁孝王拒吴楚
timeline.title_en: Prince Xiao of Liang Bars the Rebels
timeline.summary: 梁孝王城守，吴楚兵不得过梁，亚夫得以破敌。
timeline.summary_en: Prince Xiao of Liang held his walls, and the rebels could not pass; Yafu could then break them.

timeline.title: 周亚夫平吴楚
timeline.title_en: Zhou Yafu Quells Wu and Chu
timeline.summary: 太尉周亚夫坚壁昌邑，断吴粮道，三月破吴楚，余国皆平。
timeline.summary_en: Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu held fast at Changyi, cut Wu's grain route, and broke Wu and Chu within three months; the other states were settled.

timeline.title: 废栗太子
timeline.summary: 废皇太子荣为临江王，后立胶东王彻为太子。
timeline.summary_en: Crown Prince Rong was deposed as Prince of Linjiang; later Jiaodong's king Che was made heir apparent.

timeline.title: 临江王荣死
timeline.title_en: Death of the Prince of Linjiang
timeline.summary: 临江王荣坐侵庙壖地为宫，征诣中尉，自杀。
timeline.summary_en: Rong, prince of Linjiang, was summoned to the Commandant of Justice for taking temple land for a palace, and killed himself.

timeline.title: 周亚夫下狱死
timeline.summary: 丞相周亚夫以子买官器事牵连下狱，不食五日呕血死。
timeline.summary_en: Chancellor Zhou Yafu was imprisoned on charges involving his son's purchase of burial goods and died of starvation, vomiting blood on the fifth day.

timeline.title: 景帝崩
timeline.summary: 崩于未央宫，太子彻即位，是为武帝。
timeline.summary_en: He died in the Weiyang Palace; Crown Prince Che succeeded as Emperor Wu.

bio_md:
# 汉景帝 · 主要事迹

刘启是[[han-wen-di|汉文帝]]之子，以太子继位。他承文帝休养之政，减笞轻刑，本可平稳守成，却因削藩一事掀起汉初最大的内乱——七国之乱，又以铁腕平之，把中央与诸侯王的权力天平彻底扳向长安。

乱起于御史大夫晁错的削藩之议：削吴楚支郡，吴王濞、楚王戊等七国以「诛晁错」为名举兵西向。景帝一度听袁盎言，斩晁错于东市以谢吴楚，而吴楚兵不止，方知乱意不在错。此后倚梁孝王城守睢阳，任周亚夫坚壁昌邑、断吴粮道，三月破吴楚，七国皆平。经此一役，汉初分封格局名存实变，中央集权为之奠定。

平乱之后的景帝朝并不太平：废栗太子，立胶东王[[han-wu-di|刘彻]]；临江王荣被征自杀；功高震主的周亚夫终以下狱绝食而亡。史家于此多有微词，谓其刻薄寡恩、少文帝之宽仁，然就制度后果而言，削藩与集权正是武帝盛世的前提。

后三年正月，景帝崩于未央宫，太子彻即位。文景两代四十年的休养生息，至此交棒到中国历史上最具扩张性的皇帝手中；「文景之治」作为汉家基业的代名词，也在[[han-gao-zu|汉高祖]]开国与武帝开边之间，成为承上启下的枢纽。

> 参考：点校本《汉书》卷005《景帝纪》、卷006《武帝纪》、《晁错传》，《史记》吴王濞列传、绛侯世家、梁孝王世家，谭图第 2 册。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Qi was the son of

and succeeded as heir apparent. He continued Wen's policy of rest, easing flogging and lightening punishment, and might have reigned in quiet continuity — until his plan to trim the feudatories touched off the greatest civil war of early Han, the Revolt of the Seven States, which he then suppressed with an iron hand, tipping the balance between throne and feudatories decisively toward Chang'an.

The revolt began with the trimming plan of Censor-in-Chief Chao Cuo: cutting the commanderies of Wu and Chu, the kings of Wu and Chu and five other states rose and marched west under the slogan "execute Chao Cuo." Persuaded by Yuan Ang, Emperor Jing had Chao Cuo beheaded at the East Market to appease the rebels; the armies pressed on regardless, and the court saw that the revolt was never about Chao Cuo. Thereafter Jing leaned on Prince Xiao of Liang holding Suiyang, and entrusted Zhou Yafu, who held fast at Changyi, cut Wu's grain route, and broke Wu and Chu within three months; all seven states were settled. After that war, the enfeoffment order of early Han was changed in substance, and centralization was secured.

The years after the revolt were not tranquil: the heir of the Li clan was set aside in favor of Jiaodong's king

; Rong, the deposed prince of Linjiang, was summoned and died by his own hand; and Zhou Yafu, whose merit now overshadowed the throne, ended in prison, starving himself to death on the fifth day. The historians censured the emperor here — cold and ungrateful, they said, and lacking Wen's generosity — yet in institutional terms, the trimming of the feudatories and the concentration of power were exactly the precondition of Emperor Wu's golden age.

In the first month of the later third year, Emperor Jing died in the Weiyang Palace and Crown Prince Che succeeded. Four decades of Wen-Jing recuperation now passed into the hands of the most expansionist emperor in Chinese history; and "the Wen-Jing recovery," the byword for the House of Han's foundations, became the hinge between

's founding and Emperor Wu's frontier expansion.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hanshu*, ch. 5 (Benji of Emperor Jing), ch. 6 (Benji of Emperor Wu), and the biography of Chao Cuo; the *Shiji* biography of the King of Wu, the House of Zhou Bo, and the House of Liang; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2.
